text:
Neither summary contains errors. Both give the correct date, the change from two to three office days, the formal-versus-informal arrangement distinction, the Claims and Customer Contact exclusion with the early 2027 review, the equipment rule, the hot desking details and the rationale.

The user set a limit of under 120 words, and both responses go over it. By my count Response A is about 127 words and Response B about 144. B's overrun is much larger.

B does include a few extra points: team leaders set the common day, lockers, existing equipment stays, and where to direct questions. These are minor for a busy manager and cost about 17 more words, which pushes B well past the limit. A leaves out little that matters. It drops the lockers, the questions contact and the fact that existing equipment stays, and it says "each team will have a common day" without naming team leaders.

With accuracy equal, the deciding factor is adherence to the length limit and concision. A is closer to the limit and tighter, so it is the better response, even though it also slightly overshoots.

Verdict: A
